newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand adopts measures to boost weak exports.
newsitem.headline: Thailand adopts measures to boost weak exports.

text.p: A cabinet-level economic panel has approved tax measures to boost future Thai exports after acknowledging that export growth plunged to 3.8 percent in the first seven months of this year from 26.2 percent a year ago.

Government sources said the panel, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Virawan, voted for the measures late on Friday after conceding that Thailand would miss its 1996 export growth target of 10.2 percent.
The 10.2 percent target was scaled down from the 17.4 percent projection set earlier by the central bank and compares with a 23.6 percent target in 1995.
Private bankers and economists said on Friday they expected 1996 exports to increase only about 5.0 percent, the slowest pace since 1984.

The sources said the panel would tell government agencies to relax and streamline collection and refunding of value-added tax and customs tariffs for export-oriented business and adopt tax relief measures for Thailand's small commercial shipping fleet.
Bankers said the export setback would reduce Thai economic growth this year to slightly over 7.0 percent compared with 7.8 percent projected by the central bank last month and 8.6 percent in 1995.
